doc.title: George Wein interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Listening to 'The Magic Horn' with Ruby Braff and Jimmy McPartland
summary: Rowe plays a recording; Wein explains he was musical director of the TV show, with McPartland and Braff doubling for Sal Mineo's trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay. I brought a little piece of music to play for you. It might jog your memory.
It goes back quite a ways.
Ruby Braff. “The Magic Horn.” Am I playing piano there?

I must have been reading the music or something. It doesn’t sound like me. There’s a funny story about that. We had this story, “The Magic Horn” was the story of a trumpet player and I guess Sal Mineo was the young guy, and Ralph Meeker. It was a television show. And I was the musical director. I put the band together. And — God I haven’t heard that in ages — I wouldn’t have guessed that — I knew it was Ruby, because nobody plays like Ruby. And so the story was the trumpet player who plays Sal Mineo was just an average trumpet player. And then when he got the magic horn he became a great trumpet player. So I never made it out this way. I had Jimmy McPartland playing the trumpet for the Sal Mineo before he got the magic horn, and Ruby Braff playing the trumpet from after he got the magic horn. And so I never told Jimmy. He just loved being in the show. He didn’t know what was going on.

I thought Jimmy McPartland was beautiful. But Jimmy didn’t have the greatest chops in the world but he had a great musical head and he could play wonderful music. But Ruby had chops as strong as an elephant or a crocodile, he had chops. He could bite you like a crocodile too. So Ruby became the magic horn on television that Sal Mineo played. But that’s nice to find that record. That’s good.
Yeah. That’s part of our collection at the college.
